records.title: Median cycle time to complete the annual budget
records.finding: APQC reports a cross-industry median of 35 calendar days from the beginning to the end of the annual budgeting process.

records.title: Median cycle time to prepare a financial forecast
records.finding: APQC reports a cross-industry median of 11 calendar days to prepare a financial forecast.

records.title: Median cycle time to update a rolling forecast
records.finding: APQC reports a cross-industry median of five calendar days to update or revise a rolling forecast.

records.title: Average days required to reforecast
records.finding: The top 20% of AFP's agility scoring reforecast in 9.4 days, compared with 14.5 days for other respondents. Among the top group, 94% agreed or strongly agreed that FP&A uses multiple scenarios.

records.title: Spreadsheet use in planning and reporting
records.finding: Ninety-six percent of respondents used spreadsheets for planning. Ninety-three percent used spreadsheets for reporting on a daily or weekly basis.

records.title: EPM use for planning at least quarterly
records.finding: Seventy-one percent of respondents used enterprise performance management tools for planning at least quarterly, and more than half used them daily or weekly.

records.title: Data reliability and accessibility challenges
records.finding: Sixty-one percent of respondents reported moderate to significant challenges with data reliability, and 60% reported challenges with data accessibility.

records.title: Planning and reporting tool categories in quarterly use
records.finding: More than half of respondents reported using at least eight categories of planning tools and 10 types of reporting tools each quarter.

records.title: Expected growth in digital technology investment
records.finding: Ninety-six percent of respondents expected UK business investment in digital technology and assets to rise over the following five years, and 93% expected an increase over the following 12 months.
records.coverage: 58 UK CFOs, including 10 FTSE 100 and 21 FTSE 250 companies

records.title: AI use and testing within FP&A
records.finding: Twenty-three percent of respondents used AI daily, weekly, or monthly. Another 40% were testing AI and planned implementation within the following year.

records.title: Finance functions reporting AI use in 2025
records.finding: Gartner reported finance AI adoption at 59% in 2025, compared with 58% in its 2024 survey.

records.title: Leading AI use cases reported by finance functions
records.finding: In Gartner's 2024 survey, intelligent process automation was reported by 44% of finance functions and anomaly or error detection by 39%. Analytics was reported by 28% and operational assistance by 27%.

records.title: Active AI use and reported return in finance
records.finding: KPMG reported active AI use across finance at 75%, up from 30% in 2024. Seventy-one percent of respondents said AI was meeting or exceeding return expectations.

records.title: Reported AI-related finance outcomes
records.finding: Respondents reported improvement in decision speed at 71%, decision quality at 70%, and forecast accuracy at 64%.

records.title: Assurance readiness and failure tracking
records.finding: Forty-two percent of organizations were classified as fully assurance-ready for AI-enabled finance processes, while 29% tracked where AI adoption failed. Data quality was cited by 36% as both the leading barrier and opportunity.

records.title: Enterprise AI use and reported EBIT effect
records.finding: Eighty-eight percent reported regular AI use in at least one business function, while roughly one-third had begun scaling enterprise-wide. Thirty-nine percent reported any enterprise-level EBIT effect, and most of that group attributed less than 5% of EBIT to AI.

records.title: North American CFO expectations for AI in 2026
records.finding: Eighty-seven percent said AI would be extremely or very important to finance operations in 2026. Fifty-four percent identified integrating AI agents as a finance transformation priority, and 50% named digital finance transformation as a top priority.
records.coverage: 200 CFOs at North American companies with at least $1B revenue

records.title: Finance AI preparedness and investment barriers
records.finding: Twenty-one percent rated their finance function's AI preparedness as advanced or leading. Data quality and bias were cited by 61% as a top challenge in securing investment for AI tools, followed by long-term, indirect or unclear benefits at 51% and limited skills, resources or capacity at 50%.
records.coverage: 1,610 CFOs, finance directors and heads of finance; 28 countries; 22 industries

source.title: 2026 EY Global DNA of the CFO Survey

records.title: Finance workload, staffing, and budget outlook for 2026
records.finding: The Hackett Group projected finance workload growth of 3.2%, a 2.1% headcount decline, and a 1.7% budget decline, producing a stated 5.3% productivity gap. Planned technology spending increased 5.6%.
records.coverage: Respondent count not stated in public release

records.title: FP&A practitioners at or above full capacity
records.finding: Sixty-five percent of practitioners reported working at or above 100% capacity, while 54% strongly agreed that their FP&A teams were adequately staffed.

records.title: Expanded CFO scope and planned ERP replacement
records.finding: More than 70% of CFOs had expanded responsibilities beyond finance to include areas such as enterprise data and analytics, AI, and corporate strategy. Among organizations with ERP systems, 87% planned a replacement or upgrade within three years.

records.title: Finance value-creation ambition and operating capacity
records.finding: Sixty percent assigned CFOs responsibility for defining and shaping how the business creates value, while 25% said they lead investment decisions with uncertain, indirect or long-term returns. Twenty-seven percent said finance was most commonly perceived as a strategic partner in value creation, and respondents reported that 47% of their capacity was devoted to operational tasks.
records.coverage: 1,610 CFOs, finance directors and heads of finance; 28 countries; 22 industries

source.title: 2026 EY Global DNA of the CFO Survey

records.title: Turbulent or stormy global outlook
records.finding: Half of surveyed leaders and experts expected a turbulent or stormy outlook over the following two years. The share rose to 57% over 10 years, while 1% expected a calm outlook at either horizon.
records.coverage: More than 1,300 global leaders and experts

source.title: World Economic Forum Global Risks Report 2026

records.title: Organizations reporting disruption
records.finding: Ninety-one percent reported at least one disruption other than the pandemic and averaged 3.5 disruptions over two years. Seventy-six percent said their most serious disruption had a medium-to-high operational impact.

source.title: PwC Global Crisis and Resilience Survey

records.title: Confidence in recovery and strategic priority
records.finding: Seventy percent of business leaders expressed confidence in their organization's ability to recover from disruptions. Eighty-nine percent classified resilience as one of their most important strategic priorities.

source.title: PwC Global Crisis and Resilience Survey

records.title: Payments fraud and business email compromise
records.finding: Seventy-six percent of U.S. organizations experienced attempted or actual payments fraud in 2025, and 74% were affected by business email compromise. Checks were the most frequently affected payment method at 58%.

records.title: External uncertainty and geopolitical risk
records.finding: Forty-seven percent rated external financial and economic uncertainty as high or very high. Geopolitics remained the highest-rated external risk at an average of 68 out of 100, down from 79 in the first quarter of 2026.
records.coverage: 58 UK CFOs, including 10 FTSE 100 and 21 FTSE 250 companies
records.type: Survey response and average risk rating

records.title: Financial challenges reported by small employer firms
records.finding: Seventy-five percent cited rising input or wage costs, 56% cited paying operating expenses, and 51% cited uneven cash flow as financial challenges.

source.title: Federal Reserve 2025 Report on Employer Firms

records.title: Worldwide factoring volume in 2025
records.finding: FCI reported worldwide factoring turnover of €4.039 trillion in 2025, 3.7% above 2024. Europe represented 65.8% of total reported volume.

records.title: Cash or liquidity forecasting identified as a leading challenge
records.finding: More than 60% of treasury professionals identified cash or liquidity forecasting as their most challenging task. Nearly three-quarters cited cash management and forecasting as top departmental priorities.

records.title: Short-term investment objectives
records.finding: Safety was the top short-term investment objective for 61% of respondents, followed by liquidity at 35% and yield at 5%. Forty-six percent named bank products as their primary short-term investment vehicle.

records.title: Stablecoin and tokenized-product adoption
records.finding: One percent of respondents reported piloting or limited use of stablecoins and tokenized products, while 9% were actively exploring the technology.
records.coverage: 309 treasury professionals from U.S. organizations of varying sizes and industries

records.title: Cash balances and short-term investment allocation
records.finding: Forty-six percent of organizations increased their U.S. cash balances as of March 2026, up from 38% a year earlier. An average of 83% of short-term investment balances was held in safe and liquid vehicles, while the average bank-deposit share fell to 42%, its lowest level since 2011.
records.coverage: 309 treasury professionals from U.S. organizations of varying sizes and industries

records.title: Investment policy use and 24/7 liquidity expectations
records.finding: Three in four organizations had a written investment policy governing short-term investments. Forty-one percent expected money market funds to offer 24/7 liquidity, up from 38% in 2025.
records.coverage: 309 treasury professionals from U.S. organizations of varying sizes and industries

records.title: Pressure to prove AI-agent returns is outpacing measurable value
records.finding: Ninety-two percent of surveyed finance leaders reported moderate or significant career pressure to demonstrate ROI from AI-agent investments. Half said their initiatives had delivered only limited measurable ROI, 71% said deployment pressure emphasized speed, and 7% said their organization prioritized governance over speed.
records.coverage: 1,505 CFOs and senior finance leaders at companies with $10M+ revenue across the U.S., U.K., Australia, and India

source.title: Agents of Change: How the Race to Deploy AI Agents is Outrunning Financial Governance

records.title: AI-agent controls, explainability, accountability, and expertise gaps
records.finding: Thirty percent had not updated internal controls within the prior year to reflect AI agents taking or recommending actions. Forty-four percent were only somewhat confident they could explain an agent's actions to an auditor or regulator, 23% said accountability for a significant error would be unclear or sit with no one, and 76% lacked dedicated in-house expertise to understand how their agents worked.
records.coverage: 1,505 CFOs and senior finance leaders at companies with $10M+ revenue across the U.S., U.K., Australia, and India

source.title: Agents of Change: How the Race to Deploy AI Agents is Outrunning Financial Governance

records.title: Enterprise AI use is shifting from assistance to agentic execution
records.finding: As of June 2026, Codex accounted for 64% of combined Codex and ChatGPT output tokens among enterprise customers. Frontier firms generated 8.3 times as many output tokens per active user as typical firms, up from a 2.6-times gap in January. OpenAI notes that token volume is a proxy for depth of use, not a direct measure of business value.
records.coverage: OpenAI enterprise customer activity; Enterprise Signals draws on more than 10 million messages

source.title: Enterprise Signals: What frontier firms are doing differently

records.title: Frontier firms use connected AI capabilities more frequently
records.finding: Among weekly active users, 21% at frontier firms used Plugins and 19% used skills, compared with 9% and 3%, respectively, at typical firms. The figures measure capability adoption and do not by themselves establish financial return.
records.coverage: OpenAI enterprise customer activity; Enterprise Signals draws on more than 10 million messages

source.title: Enterprise Signals: What frontier firms are doing differently

records.title: Agentic work is spreading beyond engineering
records.finding: Since February, weekly active enterprise Codex users increased 108 times in legal, 41 times in sales, 41 times in recruiting, and 26 times in marketing, compared with five times in engineering. The measure reflects growth in active users rather than productivity or economic return.
records.coverage: OpenAI enterprise customer activity; Enterprise Signals draws on more than 10 million messages

source.title: From assistance to execution: How enterprises put AI to work

records.title: AI-generated finance presentations reached higher completion and readiness rates
records.finding: In Model ML's Composite evaluation, GPT-5.6 Sol produced a PowerPoint file in 100% of test cases versus 76% for Opus 5. It passed the company's professional-readiness gate in 43.3% of cases versus 26.7%. The benchmark was designed and reported by the solution provider and covered hundreds of generated decks.
records.coverage: Hundreds of generated finance decks evaluated using Model ML's internal Composite benchmark

source.title: Model ML completes finance work more efficiently with GPT-5.6 Sol

records.title: Finance-workbook efficiency improved, while full-model correctness remained mixed
records.finding: In Model ML's native Excel benchmark, GPT-5.6 Sol used 36% fewer tokens per workbook than Opus 5 and achieved 83.3% headline-output accuracy. However, 50% of its workbooks had every key output correct, compared with 60% for Opus 5, Fable 5, and GPT-5.5. The result separates efficiency and partial accuracy from end-to-end correctness.
records.coverage: Model ML Composite finance-workbook evaluation; exact workbook count not stated on the published page

source.title: Model ML completes finance work more efficiently with GPT-5.6 Sol
